e2e-23191782-season-7686105.tracking: Registered here. The boundary is deliberate and published in three places — bilibili-asr-archive/README.md L301 ('feeds nothing below it'), docs/metadata-storage.md L288-305 ('the two paths do not feed each other yet'), and the iter-2026-09-bilibili-api-sqlite compass 'Out of scope' list — so this registers a known deferred capability, not a defect. Operator decision 2026-09-17: register only, no code change now ('只登记 residual，暂不动'). **2026-09-19 SURVEY CORRECTION (three registration errors, all verified at HEAD 887ef0e):** (1) the README anchor is **L333**, not L301 — the quoted sentence ('feeds nothing below it') is present, just 32 lines lower; docs/metadata-storage.md L288-305 is exact and its Boundary heading is real. (2) The queue attribution was wrong and is fixed in `scope`: `no-subtitle` lives in `acquisition_attempts.outcome` (schema-transcripts.sql:76) and surfaces through the `v_pending_subtitles` view (schema-transcripts.sql:106), read by `list_pending_subtitle_parts` / `count_pending_subtitle_parts` (database.py:1091/1125). `video_parts.processing_status` (models.py:15/24) cannot hold that value; only `_cmd_status` reads it (cli.py:1223). (3) 'documented non-goal of iter-2026-09-bilibili-api-sqlite' is only two-thirds true: that compass's Out-of-scope list excludes migration/import, audio download and ASR execution — it never names this bridge; the closest statement is its No-Migration Declaration. The title was softened accordingly. **Substance re-verified and unchanged:** all six ASR-chain handlers construct only `ManifestStore` (download-audio cli.py:1072-1099, asr :1696-1700, pilot :1974-1988, campaign :2266/2393-2400, run :2425-2433, schedule :2524-2553) with zero hits for archive.db/Database/Repository/storage across their spans; no ASR-chain module imports the storage layer; the only cross-store projection runs the OTHER way (cli.py:1280-1281, manifest to SQLite, used by status/runs); `storage/` contains no srt/txt/md reference at all. **Where the gap actually is (sizes the work honestly):** piece 1 (enumerate the audio queue from SQLite) has the SQL already but **no CLI wiring**; piece 2 (rebuild SRT/TXT/MD from stored transcripts) is **absent entirely** — the data is in `transcripts`/`transcript_segments`, `archive.write_archive` already renders segments to the three files, so what is missing is the command joining them plus a stem/version-identity decision (`list_transcript_versions`); piece 3 (give the legacy audio feeder a source) is confirmed absent (`needs_audio` is written only by subtitles.py:129 via _cmd_pilot, while harvest-subs goes through services.subtitle_ingest). **Cheapest corpus-unblocking slice is pieces 1+3, S-sized** (synthesize manifest rows `work_id = bvid:p{page}` from video_parts + v_pending_subtitles, or add `download-audio --from-sqlite`); the full three-piece closure is M-sized and should be staged. **2026-09-19 Phase-1 RECON — this row's own wording was wrong a second time and is now corrected in `scope`:** the earlier edit said v_pending_subtitles is "keyed on acquisition_attempts.outcome = 'no-subtitle'"; that string appears in NO SQL file. The view's predicate is absence of any transcript row plus processing_status <> 'gone' (schema-transcripts.sql:138-141), so never-attempted and failed parts are equally pending. A queue built from the old wording would have excluded precisely the fresh backlog it exists to serve. **What the recon established (all anchored, HEAD cf3f779):** (a) video_parts is the part identity (UNIQUE(bvid,page_index), surrogate video_part_id; cid stored but not unique) and work_id is COMPUTED in three separate views (schema.sql:128,159; schema-transcripts.sql:124) while Python computes the same form independently in page_identity.format_work_id — nothing enforces agreement. (b) transcripts.source_kind already allows 'asr-local' with a nullable model_id, and the partial content-uniqueness index explicitly leaves asr-local's per-model/run identity rule open with the comment that 'that decision belongs to the audio/ASR iteration' (schema-transcripts.sql:30-35) — an invitation this iteration should accept or explicitly decline. (c) acquisition_attempts.outcome is caption-only and its CHECK binds outcome to transcript_id/error_code, so per-part audio/ASR evidence has no home without a schema change; acquisition_runs.kind already accepts 'audio' and 'asr', so run-level rows need none. (d) The schema policy forbids migration: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS cannot widen a constraint and an existing archive.db 'keeps the shape it has' (schema-transcripts.sql:4-10) — any widening applies to fresh databases only. (e) audio_objects / part_audio_objects / asr_models are declared-intentionally-empty scaffolding referenced by tests only, so a 'has audio' query over them runs clean and returns the whole corpus. (f) Rotation is a repository-level ORDER BY contract, not schema (database.py:1091-1123, 'the locked contract the CLI reads'), and it depends on per-part attempt evidence audio cannot currently record — a naive 'no audio row' queue has no recency column and would re-attempt the same head every bounded run. (g) The NOT EXISTS in v_pending_subtitles has no source_kind filter, so writing an asr-local transcript silently drains the subtitle backlog and changes what count_pending_subtitle_parts means. (h) v_pending_metadata is a second, unrelated 'pending' notion one function name away (MetadataRepository.list_pending_parts = metadata NOT yet collected) and the CLI's only backlog line already prints it under the bare label 'pending:' — a naming trap a plan must avoid. (i) On the manifest side, needs_audio's only writer was the legacy harvest path that harvest-subs bypassed, no code sets pending/meta_ok/sub_checked, and upsert rejects a new row without a page-qualified work_id — so no code path can birth a manifest row today. (j) The ASR chain reads subtitle segments from the FILESYSTEM (subtitles/raw/{stem}.json), not from transcript_segments, so a synthesized subtitle_done row would reach the archive stage and skip with missing_subtitle_raw. (k) duration_s (not duration_ms) is load-bearing for the audio budget and fails closed: a row without a converted duration skips every download. (l) Injection seams already exist: CampaignRunner(scope_rows=...), _run_scope_rows(store, entries, scope) and RunCoordinator.run_batch([(key, entry)]) — a bridge does not have to restructure routing. **2026-09-19 Phase-1 RECON, second finding — the blast radius is wider than this row states.** The row's 'two command families' framing implies the manifest family is the six ASR-chain commands, but four more readers touch manifest-shaped state: `coverage` (cli.py:1497, ReaderPolicy from sidecar_projection), `coverage --quality` (cli.py:1280-1281, reads manifest/manifest.jsonl directly), `verify` (cli.py:2969, sidecar_projection) and `export` (writes a manifest-shaped file, README:353). The closed R2 row named three of them as project_manifest_records consumers. Consequence for planning: any plan that changes manifest semantics must treat those four as affected interfaces, and the frozen spec's cross-layer no-import rule (only cli composes) plus the single-writer boundary (coordinator/archive-writer.lock) are hard constraints on where a bridge may live. **Also recorded from the recon's paper-trail pass:** the split is a SETTLED decision, not a defect — docs/metadata-storage.md:302-305 enumerates the three next-iteration pieces verbatim, bilibili-asr-archive-cli.md:242-244 assigns ownership ('deferred work owned by the audio/ASR iteration'), and no-migration is settled four separate times. 20260922-proofread-wave.title: **The ASR hotword list is also an insertion source.** A token from the run's own `provenance.hotwords` is written into the transcript where the speaker said something else — measured in **6 of 6** proofread items, including **two cases where the transcriber/corrector completed the hotword phrase with a character that appears in neither source**. The project's own hotword scoring counts *surface occurrences*, so it cannot separate a recovered term from an inserted one: the corpus-wide count that made the ASR look like the stronger system on domain vocabulary is contaminated.
20260922-proofread-wave.source: Proofreading wave, 2026-09-22 (six items, 7.30 h of audio, UID 23191782; each item read against both machine transcripts by an independent seat and then audited by a second, independent seat). Decisive criterion used throughout: the token is in the run's `provenance.hotwords` **and** the live AI caption over the same span is unrelated text **and** the ASR confidence there is low. Measured instances: `国际劳工仲裁` **13× on ASR sides vs 0× on any caption side** across the six items (e.g. ASR「但是国际劳工仲裁，它和一个东西没有关系」vs caption「但是所有人哈姆拉加起来他和一个东西没有关系」); `未明子` ≥9× (replacing 为你 / 我也知道 / 或者说); `马恩牌` 3× (replacing the deliberate character-split joke 马叉虫); `齐泽克` (replacing 骑在头上), `黑格尔`, `主义主义`, `根正苗红`, and the English string `International Employment Matters Tribunal`. Fabrications (a character present in neither source, added to complete a hotword): `BV1vNTqzFEve 00:05:55` ASR「就这么正苗红」+ caption「就这么这么简单」→ shipped 「就这么**根正苗红**」; and `BV1BdtazGEBE 00:15:50` (same class, caught only by the repair seat's own sweep). Negative control that keeps this honest: `拉康`/`辩证法`/`此在`/`实存` in the same list are **caption-attested** at their spans and were correctly kept — a hotword hit is not automatically an insertion. Reporting detail: the E2E's own hotword figure ("ASR 2–17 hits per item vs caption 0–3") counted occurrences, which is why it read as a win; the corrected statement is that an unknown share of those hits are insertions.
20260922-proofread-wave.scope: The decoder's hotword prior and every consumer of it, including the project's own measurement of the feature. Two legs: (a) **the transcript product** — an operator reading an archived transcript cannot tell a spoken term from an injected one, which is the archive's core value proposition; (b) **the measurement** — `hotword-list-measurement.md`'s family of measurements scores a hotword by its presence in the output, so a hotword that raises the score by hallucinating counts the same as one that raises it by correcting. Closers for (a): ship the hotword list as a *soft* prior with an insertion guard (e.g. require the token to survive a second decode, or gate it on the caption when a caption exists), or record per-token provenance so a consumer can see which terms came from the prior; for (b): score with a **caption-conditioned** or insertion-penalised metric that separates recovery from injection, and re-measure the existing shard results under it. Closing condition: one of those lands and the corpus-level measurement is restated with insertions counted separately.

20260922-proofread-wave.title: **A source-reducing formatting step was not count-guarded, and it silently narrowed what six reviewers could see.** The alignment table I built for the proofreading wave assigned each caption cue to an ASR-derived time block by its **midpoint**; a cue whose midpoint fell between blocks (i.e. inside an ASR VAD gap) belonged to no block and was **dropped from the table entirely** — 251 of 9607 cues (2.6%), with no `⟨空缺⟩` marker and no count check.
20260922-proofread-wave.source: Measured 2026-09-22 during and after the proofreading wave. Root cause: `blocks()` derives block spans from ASR segments only, and each caption cue is attached by `block.start <= cue_midpoint < block.end`; a cue in a VAD gap matches no block. Corpus result: 251/9607 cues dropped (BV1BdtazGEBE 66, BV1iddQYQE7D 82, BV1vNTqzFEve 56, BV1Y7M4zNEfF 21, BV1zz5zzFENq 15, BV11p5qzAE6s 11). Independent confirmation: the reviewer for `BV1zz5zzFENq` reported, without knowing the cause, that the caption column was “a lossier capture than the raw caption JSON at the same publish path — 15 clause-drops / 186 chars” — exactly my measurement for that item. **Only after the repair seats worked the lists item by item did the real content cost become measurable: 13 short utterances added (BV1BdtazGEBE 3, BV1iddQYQE7D 6, BV1vNTqzFEve 2, BV1zz5zzFENq 1, others 0) plus 1 marked**; the remaining dropped cues were carried by adjacent ASR segments that were in the table. My first estimate (100 cues “missing from both”) was an upper bound from a substring test and was wrong by roughly an order of magnitude — the corrected figure is the 13 above.
20260922-proofread-wave.scope: Verification methodology, not product code: any transformation that sits **between a source and the person or agent judging it** and can lose source text without saying so. This instance was ad-hoc tooling for one E2E, so the durable form of the lesson is a rule, not a patch: a source-reducing step must (a) account for every input item (count in == count out, with an explicit bucket for “not attached”), (b) never render a dropped item as silence. It sits in the same family as `{KNOWLEDGE_DIR}/best-practices/premise-freshness-before-lock.md` (a premise inherited rather than re-verified) and the E2E's own `absence-assertion-negative-control` discipline. Closers: record the rule where the project's verification methodology lives (a best-practice note or the E2E contract), or nothing — accepted as a closed one-off with the measurement above as its record.
